A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. EVOKE is renamed MMEVOKE, with the core benchmark and experiments readily matched. Both complete PDFs, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-injection experiments, capability evaluations, and augmentation and continual-learning analyses in Tables 1–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds human quality ratings, reasoning-task evaluations, augmentation comparisons, and knowledge-editing results.

M1.justification: v2 Section 5.1 extends augmentation with additional real-world images of the same entity and a mechanical text-augmentation control. v1 used text paraphrases and conventional image transformations. The benchmark-construction pipeline, model architectures, and core fine-tuning and retrieval procedures remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The core News/Entity benchmark and twelve general-capability benchmarks are retained. Appendix B.6 adds evaluated counterfactual and three-hop questions alongside corresponding original SimpleVQA questions, substantially extending reasoning requirements beyond the original single-hop evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-4.1 to web-search and sufficient-context comparisons, and FT-LLM, FT-VIS, RECIPE, LTE, and LiveEdit in Appendix H. Augmentation variants enter the general-capability comparison. The instruction-violation analysis drops LoRA. Golden Context is retained under the name Sufficient Context.

E3.justification: New designs include a 100-sample quality audit with four annotators using 1–5 ratings, the reported 568-pair reasoning extension, and editing evaluations at 10, 1,000, 2,000, and 4,000 edits. Visual augmentation is now evaluated specifically on Entity data. Accuracy becomes CEM, but its stated containment-based scoring rule is unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds benchmark-quality validation, reasoning-difficulty analysis, augmentation effects on general capabilities, sufficient-context error analysis, and reasoning-consistency/factual-grounding cases. Sequential fine-tuning and retrieval ablations are retained. The earlier inference-time augmentation analyses and LoRA training-loss plot are omitted.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces uncertainty notation for human ratings, including Q&A quality of 4.86 ± 0.01; v1 has no corresponding reporting. The meaning of these ± quantities is unspecified, and model-run counts, seeds, and significance testing remain unreported.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive commercial-model, reasoning, editing, augmentation, and subfield results while retaining most original headline scores. New sufficient-context CEM scores include GPT-4.1 at 75.02 and Gemini-2.5-Pro at 72.15. Existing results also change: Replay Full-FT overall accuracy/CEM is 10.43 in v1 Table 3 and 11.07 in v2 Table 10, without an explained experimental change.

T1.justification: The injection/evaluation data definitions, knowledge-adaptation and retention objectives, and answer-containment scoring definition remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The augmentation contribution changes from text helping while conventional image augmentation fails to knowledge-aware augmentation helping both text and entity images, with partial capability-retention benefits. v2 also elevates a consistent cross-capability degradation ranking to a main contribution, while retaining the central findings of poor injection performance and capability loss.

C2.justification: v2 develops interpretations linking sufficient-context failures to reasoning and context utilization, and contrasts knowledge rehearsal and separation with rigid regularization. Its conclusion shifts from internet augmentation and scaling concerns toward combining semantic augmentation with retention methods. Appendix E.2 adds discussion of augmentation's remaining instruction-following, dialogue, and reasoning weaknesses.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page/code-and-data availability statement, manual-inspection timing, quarterly-update information, and disclosure of LLM judging. It removes v1's paraphrase-generation prompt and examples, and the disclosure that Perplexity results used 2,000 manually tested examples. These are documentation changes, not evidence that the retained experiments used different settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against temporal-knowledge benchmarks, including Realtime QA, DyKnow, and EvoWiki. Appendix H introduces a broader relationship to multimodal and lifelong knowledge editing, while the continual-learning discussion is updated to emphasize factual knowledge adaptation and retention.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark description, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. EVOKE becomes MMEVOKE, Pathways becomes Explorations, and capability degradation replaces much catastrophic-forgetting terminology. Main sections and appendices are substantially reorganized around research questions, observations, challenges, and insights.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, redesigns motivation and augmentation figures, and adds statistics, validation, reasoning, and editing displays. Detailed numerical capability tables in v1 Appendix E become radar plots without numerical axis labels in v2 Appendix D. Several unchanged ablation plots and generation prompts are relocated.

improvement.justification: The human quality audit, reasoning-task checks, and semantic-versus-mechanical augmentation comparisons provide better support for benchmark validity and refine v1's broad text-versus-image conclusion. These gains are tempered by lost sampling and prompt disclosures, reduced numerical transparency in the appendix radar plots, and Appendix E.2's overly broad augmentation-superiority claim despite mixed results in Table 3. The net improvement is therefore limited.
